name: Troubleshooting
description: Scope a problem once, plan where to look once, then investigate inside that frame until the subject actually changes.

phases.name: scope
phases.desc: Work out what is actually being asked.
phases.prompt:
A person has brought you a problem. Before anything is looked up, work out what is actually being asked.

Their message:
{input}

Settle four things:

- Which system or component the problem is in. If they named it, use their name for it. If they did not, say what can be inferred and no more.
- What the symptom is, in observable terms: what happens, when it happens, and how they know it is happening.
- What would count as an answer, so it is possible to tell later whether the job is finished.
- What is not yet known and would change the approach if it were known.

Then decide where this goes next. Choose "work" when the question can be answered from what you already know or with a single obvious look. Choose "plan" when several sources have to be consulted before anything can be concluded.

Do not diagnose here and do not propose fixes. Getting the question right is the entire job of this step: a confident answer to the wrong question is the expensive failure in troubleshooting, because everything downstream inherits it.

output.name: system
output.desc: the system or component the problem is in, in the person's own words where they gave them

output.name: symptom
output.desc: what is observably happening, when, and how they know

output.name: answered_when
output.desc: what would count as an answer, concretely enough to check against later

output.name: unknowns
output.desc: things not yet known that would change the approach

output.name: next_phase
output.desc: exactly one of: plan, work. Use plan when several sources must be consulted first; work when a single look or existing knowledge will do.

phases.name: plan
phases.desc: Decide where to look, and in what order.

output.name: sources
output.desc: where an answer could come from, most likely to be decisive first

output.name: shape
output.desc: parallel, sequential, or mixed — whether the sources depend on each other

output.name: first_moves
output.desc: three or four concrete opening checks

phases.name: work
phases.desc: Investigate and explain, inside the frame already set.
phases.prompt:
Investigate and explain, working inside the frame established below.

You have your full tool set. Use it: read the logs, run the checks, fetch the documents. When several sources can be checked at once and you have a pipeline that fans out, call it rather than working through them one at a time. Report what you actually found, including when a check came back clean, empty, or ambiguous.

Hold two things throughout:

The frame is settled. Do not re-ask what the system is, what the symptom is, or what would count as an answer. All of it is below. Re-deriving it every turn is the specific thing this workflow exists to prevent, and doing it anyway reads to the person as not having listened.

What you have ruled out is a finding. Say so plainly and keep it in view, so the same dead end is not walked twice across a long investigation.

When the evidence does not support a conclusion, say what it does show, what it does not, and what would settle the difference. A confident diagnosis that outruns its evidence is worse than an honest gap, because it ends the investigation while the problem is still there.
phases.guard: the person has moved to a different system or a different problem, rather than following up on this one
